title: When the Horizon Breaks
premise: Ines Nakamura, estranged daughter of disgraced archaeologist Kenji Nakamura, is salvaging her own reputation on the coast of Isla Verde when a storm tide exposes a sea cave concealing the wreck of the Meridian Star — and evidence that her father's career was destroyed to bury its discovery. Racing a salvage fleet backed by the corrupt magistrate who ruined him, Ines has six tides before the concession permits expire to recover proof of the find and her father's innocence. Betrayed by an ally, nearly drowned, and forced to choose between the treasure that would restore her name and the truth that would destroy the man who destroyed her father, she wins the race but loses the fortune — trading gold for testimony that finally breaks the magistrate. The novel ends with Ines walking away from the horizon with something rarer than treasure: a legacy she chose herself.
about_author: Vesper Halloran is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent a decade mapping shipwrecks off Pacific coastlines before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who out-navigate both storms and institutions.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Its Own Books
chapters.summary: Ines Nakamura works a private dig on Isla Verde's cliffs, scraping a living from other people's discarded permits. POV: Ines. Establishes her competence, her debt, and her bitterness toward her father. Emotional beat: weary self-reliance masking grief.

chapters.title: A Letter Six Years Late
chapters.summary: Ines receives a letter from Kenji Nakamura asking her to meet him at the old survey station — postmarked the week before his death. POV: Ines. She almost burns it; instead she packs her kit. Emotional beat: anger cracking open into longing.

chapters.title: The Storm That Gives Back
chapters.summary: A violent northeaster scours the coastline overnight. At dawn, Ines finds a sea cave exposed below the cliffs, its mouth littered with timbers stamped MERIDIAN STAR. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as she recognizes the legendary lost wreck.

chapters.title: Legends Charge Admission
chapters.summary: Ines explores the cave's outer chamber and finds a sealed strongbox bearing her father's survey marks — he found this first, years ago, and told no one but someone who betrayed him. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the letter's meaning begins to sharpen into accusation.

chapters.title: The Concession
chapters.summary: Magistrate Aurelio Vance announces emergency salvage concessions on the newly exposed site, awarding them to the Corvus Fleet — owned by his brother-in-law. Ines realizes the six-tide clock has started without her. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: cold fury at a rigged game.

chapters.title: What My Father Taught Me
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Ines learning tide tables and sediment reading from Kenji, and the fight that estranged them. POV: Ines (past). Emotional beat: understanding that he taught her everything except how to forgive him.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ines calculates the window: six usable tides before spring tides reseal the cave and the permits consolidate Corvus's claim. She decides to beat the fleet inside. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Diver Who Owes Everyone
chapters.summary: Ines recruits Teo Brandt, a disgraced salvage diver who once worked for Corvus and knows their methods — and their captain, Mara Voss. POV: Teo. Introduces his debts and his hunger for one clean job. Emotional beat: shame looking for redemption.

chapters.title: First Descent
chapters.summary: Teo dives the cave's flooded inner passage while Ines runs lines from above. He reaches an air pocket and surfaces beside rows of intact cargo crates. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: wonder — then terror at hearing engines: the fleet has arrived early.

chapters.title: Mara Voss
chapters.summary: Captain Voss surveys the site from the Corvus flagship, under orders from Vance to recover the manifest first and let the 'accident' of history handle the rest. POV: Mara. Reveals she suspects what Vance buried. Emotional beat: professional loyalty beginning to itch.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Ines and Teo breach a lead-lined chest containing the Meridian Star's true manifest — cargo lists that contradict every official record, including the report that ended Kenji's career. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: vindication arriving hand in hand with danger.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed the Report
chapters.summary: Ines deciphers annotations in the manifest in Vance's handwriting, dated years before he held office — he falsified the original survey. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief for her father reframed as purpose.

chapters.title: Corvus Moves
chapters.summary: Voss's divers begin pumping the outer chamber. Ines and Teo must work in the fleet's shadow, hiding their finds in a cliff cache. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension, near-discovery by a Corvus diver.

chapters.title: Third Tide: The Captain's Log
chapters.summary: They recover the Meridian Star's logbook, revealing the ship was deliberately scuttled to hide embezzled colonial funds — money that built half the island's old families, including Vance's. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: history as a weapon.

chapters.title: An Offer on the Water
chapters.summary: Voss intercepts Ines's skiff and offers her a cut to walk away, revealing she knows exactly who Ines is. Ines refuses. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grudging respect between adversaries.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Air Goes Bad
chapters.summary: A collapse shifts the cave's air pocket; Teo is trapped behind falling rock with a failing regulator. Ines performs a desperate solo rescue through the flooded passage. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: trust forged in near-death.

chapters.title: What Teo Buried
chapters.summary: Convalescing, Teo confesses he was the Corvus diver on the original cover-up dive years ago — the one who reported Kenji's find as worthless. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: guilt offered like an open wound.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Vault Room
chapters.summary: Behind the cargo hold they find the captain's personal vault: ledgers naming every conspirator, plus letters proving Kenji tried to expose them all and was silenced professionally, not killed. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: relief and fresh rage — her father lives, broken and exiled.

chapters.title: The Choice of Gold
chapters.summary: The vault also holds the embezzled specie itself — enough to erase Ines's debts forever. Carrying it means slowing down; leaving it means losing it to Corvus. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: temptation weighed against inheritance of a different kind.

chapters.title: Vance Comes Down the Cliff
chapters.summary: Magistrate Vance arrives personally, uneasy about Voss, and orders the cave sealed early with explosives — permits be damned. POV: Vance. Villain POV reveals his panic and his contempt for everyone, including Voss. Emotional beat: banal evil under pressure.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Cache
chapters.summary: Their cached finds are gone — Teo's old crewmate Renn, whom Teo trusted, sold the location to Corvus. The manifest survives only because Ines kept copies on her body. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: betrayal confirming his worst beliefs about himself.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Voss detains Ines aboard the flagship, probing what she knows. Ines turns the interrogation around, planting doubt about Vance's plans for Voss as expendable. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: two sharp women recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Escape on the Ebb
chapters.summary: Ines escapes during a supply transfer, swimming the ebb current to shore with the logbook waterproofed against her chest. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: exhaustion transformed into ferocity.

chapters.title: The Island's Memory
chapters.summary: Ines brings the documents to Doña Imelda Cruz, matriarch of a family named in the ledgers, hoping shame will buy an ally. Instead Imelda offers something better: the island's oral history corroborating the scuttling. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: justice needing more than paper.

chapters.title: Renn's Price
chapters.summary: Teo confronts Renn, learns Vance ordered the theft and promised Renn a stake — and overhears that Vance plans to sink the Corvus flagship with Voss aboard once the vault is recovered, erasing all witnesses. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: loyalty redirected.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide Approaches
chapters.summary: The final spring tide looms; after it, the cave seals for a generation and the permits vest fully in Corvus. Everything must happen now. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: ticking-clock dread.

chapters.title: Alliances of Convenience
chapters.summary: Ines, Teo, and Voss — warned by Teo — meet secretly and form an uneasy pact: get the evidence out, expose Vance, split nothing but survival. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: enemies becoming comrades under a common threat.

chapters.title: The Plan of Three Currents
chapters.summary: They plan a three-pronged operation: Voss stalls the demolition crew, Teo recovers the vault contents via the underwater passage, Ines carries the documents overland to the mainland ferry and the press. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: Vance's crew begins setting charges early. Voss sabotages the detonators and buys hours at the cost of being arrested by her own first mate, bought by Vance. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: sacrifice as command.

chapters.title: Last Dive
chapters.summary: Teo makes the final run through the collapsing passage as charges crack the cavern, hauling out the ledgers and — after a suspended breath — leaving the gold behind to make weight. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: redemption priced in gold, paid gladly.

chapters.title: The Overland Run
chapters.summary: Ines races cross-island with the documents, hunted by Renn and Vance's men through mangrove and karst, using every tracking skill her father taught her. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the wilderness forgiving nothing, forgetting less — and finally taking her side.

chapters.title: Renn at the Ford
chapters.summary: Renn corners Ines at a river ford. She defeats him not with violence but with the truth of what Vance promised versus what Vance does to loose ends — and lets him choose. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Dawn
chapters.summary: Ines reaches the ferry dock as Vance's launch closes in; the mainland papers' correspondent, tipped by Imelda, is aboard. She hands over the ledgers as Vance's men board. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the handoff as climax-in-miniature.

chapters.title: Climax: The Cave Comes Down
chapters.summary: Vance detonates the remaining charges to destroy the site and the last physical proof — but the blast collapses on his own men and exposes the vault room to the arriving press and naval inspector, documenting everything. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: the architect buried by his blueprint.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Voss, released when her mutinous first mate defects, testifies; Renn corroborates; the ledgers do the rest. Vance is taken into federal custody as the permits are voided. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: justice outside the law finally entering it.

chapters.title: What the Sea Kept
chapters.summary: Ines returns to the ruined cave at low water. Most of the treasure is gone or buried beyond reach — and she finds she doesn't mind. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: letting go of the gold, keeping the truth.

chapters.title: The Man in the Exile Town
chapters.summary: Ines travels inland to find Kenji alive, old and diminished, running a tiny museum of nothing much. Their reunion is awkward, unfinished, real. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: forgiveness begun, not concluded.

chapters.title: The Meridian Reopened
chapters.summary: Months later, a legitimate archaeological consortium reopens the site with Ines as lead salvor and Teo as dive master; Voss captains their vessel. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed on honest terms.

chapters.title: When the Horizon Breaks
chapters.summary: On the first morning of the new expedition, Ines watches dawn fracture over the water where the Meridian Star sleeps, carrying her father's tide tables and her own name signed to the permit. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: arrival — the horizon breaking open instead of her.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Letter Answered
chapters.summary: Ines writes a reply to her father's six-year-old letter and mails it to his new address, one street away. Some tides take a long time to turn. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
